intro: This is the Stadium at Perge, from the second half of the 1st century AD, and one of the best-preserved stadiums in Anatolia. Its seating is carried on seventy vaults: every third one an entrance, the rest shops. At the north end it closes in a horseshoe; the south end is left open.
spot-1: Now you are looking at the track, the running floor itself: about 20 metres wide and 234 long. Imagine the runners racing down its length.
spot-2: Now you are looking at the seating. There are eleven rows on each side, and each row is 43.6 centimetres high.
spot-3: Now you are looking at the closed north end. Here the stadium closes in a horseshoe, and the rows run round it unbroken.
spot-4: Now you are looking at the open south end. This end of the track was left open, and it was here that the monumental entrance stood.
spot-5: Now you are looking at the vaults. Seventy of them carry the seats: every third is an entrance, and the others are shops.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. The length, the width, the row count and the height of a row come from the Turkish Wikipedia; the 0.63 m tread the source gives and the width of the track, 20.1 m, are derived from them. The outer arches of the seventy vaults, their shops and the passages inside the north end appear only as entrance mouths. And while the open south end follows the source, the form of the monumental entrance there is unknown, so it is not drawn.
